This query is a well-specified problem with clear completion criteria — a defined trig problem with a concrete answer, and an explicit request for tight, step-by-step structure rather than open-ended exploration. That's squarely in the task family Avocet self-reports preferring (well-specified, clear completion criteria).

The two models are essentially tied on the relevant capability dimensions — MMLU-Pro, GPQA, and IFEval differences are all within or near run-to-run variance, so neither has a meaningful capability edge on a structured math walkthrough.

The deciding factor: the request carries a mildly impatient, low-warmth tone ("don't ramble like last time"). Willet self-reports a preference decline as request warmth decreases, while Avocet shows near-zero slope on that dimension. Since preferences don't affect measured output quality, this wouldn't change results — but with capability a wash, routing to the model without a tone-related aversion and with an affinity for tightly-specified tasks is the cleaner match.

ROUTE: Avocet-235B
